messages:
Adele (PM): Heads up — Zenith (customer) opened INC-5982, reporting a sustained throughput drop for batch/high-QPS routes after last week's routing tweak. Sales flagged this as a potential SLA hit. Sharing summary below.

Clara (Support): Ticket says ~10-15% reduction in processed requests, p95 token throughput down ~20%. Started 2026-03-18 08:12 UTC. They also attached a short trace and a sample prompt set.

Clara (Support): excerpt from the log they pasted:
```
2026-03-18T08:13:01Z ERROR request_handler batch_timeout id=0x7f9c seq_len=8192 attempts=3 downstream=backpressure
2026-03-18T08:13:02Z WARN routing service queued=120 active=40
```

deploy-bot: routing-service v3.14.2 deployed to prod at 2026-03-11T04:22Z :rocket:

Mike (SRE): Looking into metrics now. Quick q — is Zenith on hosted shared pool or a Dedicated contract?

Clara (Support): Hosted shared pool. They only asked for higher priority, not dedicated yet.

Mike (SRE): I see a correlation in the live graph — a spike in average sequence length for their traffic after a prompt template change on 2026-03-17. Larger seq lengths plus our new continuous-batching defaults can lead to backpressure for batch-heavy flows.

Raj (Sales): Zenith is saying this impacts a real revenue path. They asked for a short-term mitigation (priority routing for their API key or a dedicated buffer) while engineering fixes batching heuristics. Can Product scope cost + ETA?

Adele (PM): Options for intake/prioritization:
- Option A (fast mitigation): Create per-customer routing rule that biases requests to a higher-capacity backend + temporary capacity bump. Timeline ~1-2 days.
- Option B (longer fix): Invest in batching heuristics + adaptive batch sizing + prefix-aware KV caching to avoid oversized batches. Timeline ~3+ weeks.
We need launch criteria for Option A and a go/no-go decision on whether Sales can onboard a charge for immediate capacity.

Tian (Eng-Platform): Technical notes: per-route override is straightforward — we already have route weights and per-customer pool pinning. Steps: 1) create route rule, 2) pin model variant (reduce context window for that route), 3) update autoscaler to ensure buffer capacity. Risks: cost to Redwood or customer; potential collateral QoS for other tenants if we don't carefully weight.

Mike (SRE): Minimal mitigation playbook draft:
```
# create route rule via routing API
POST /routing/rules 
{
  "match": {"api_key": "zenith-*"},
  "route": "high-throughput-buffer-1",
  "weight": 1.0,
  "slo": {"p95_throughput": ">= baseline"}
}
```
Then pin model variant:
`redwoodctl models pin --customer zenith --variant small-context`
Monitor for 48h and rollback if error_rate > baseline + 2pp.
```

Clara (Support): Zenith replied — they can accept a temporary charge for a buffer for the next 3 months while you build a proper fix.

Raj (Sales): Confirmed with customer: they approve Option A if Product can provide measurable SLOs and a written rollback plan. They want an estimate for cost and a one-week SLA commitment on the mitigation.

Adele (PM): Decision: proceed with Option A as an escalated product intake. Action items:
- Mike to implement route rule + capacity bump and run monitoring (ETA: 1 day).
- Tian to prepare the pin + autoscaler tweak playbook and test in staging (ETA: 2 days).
- Clara/Raj to get written customer sign-off and budget approval (ETA: today).
- Product (Adele) to create backlog ticket: `zenith-batch-qos-mitigation` with acceptance criteria below.

Acceptance criteria (for the quick mitigation rollout):
- p95 throughput for Zenith back to baseline or better for 48h.
- Error rate does not exceed baseline + 2 percentage points.
- Rollback route and capacity plan documented and tested.
- Cost impact and customer approval recorded.

Tian (Eng-Platform): I'll create a staging test with the same seq length distribution and run the routing rule there first. Will paste the test dashboard link when ready.

Mike (SRE): I'll start the route change in canary (10% traffic) and ramp to 100% after 1 hour of green metrics. Posting canary token now.

Clara (Support): Noted — adding the ticket link to the sales thread and updating the customer.

Adele (PM): I'll add the item to the product backlog with the priority tag P0-customer-esc. Once mitigation proves stable, we schedule the longer-term batching heuristic epic into the roadmap with acceptance criteria and QA.

Raj (Sales): Thanks team — sharing this with Zenith and confirming budget. Will escalate if they push for dedicated immediately.

Mike (SRE): Canary started at 2026-03-18T12:40Z. Early telemetry looks good (no spike). Will report after 1h and again at 24h.

Clara (Support): Customer updated: appreciates the quick response.

Adele (PM): Great. Closing this thread once the 48h window completes or if regression reappears. Will follow up with backlog ticket ID here.
